cases.exposure_context_quote: A forty-year-old male was admitted to the emergency department after ingesting pesticide along with alcohol four hours earlier with suicidal intent.
cases.agent: Amitraz (identified by patient's relatives; sold in organic solvents, mostly xylene); amount UNVERIFIED
cases.agent_quote: The pesticide responsible for the poisoning was identified as “Amitraz” by the patient’s relatives.
cases.circumstance: deliberate ingestion with suicidal intent; unknown compound identified as Amitraz by relatives; clinicians used online research for treatment options

symptoms.quote: On arrival, he was found unconscious with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of three (E1V1M1).
His heart rate was 34 beats per minute, with the cardiac monitor displaying sinus bradycardia
his blood pressure measured 80/50 mm Hg.

symptoms.finding: respiratory depression; SpO2 68% in room air improving to 96% with 12 L oxygen; bilateral basal crepitations (likely pulmonary oedema)
symptoms.quote: The respiratory rate was 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation was 68% in room air, improving to 96% with 12 liters of oxygen supplementation. Bilateral basal crepitations were noted on auscultation.

symptoms.finding: pupils normal size and equally reactive
symptoms.quote: His bedside glucose was 119 mg/dL, and pupils were normal in size and equally reactive to light.

labs.name: serum magnesium
labs.quote: The patient exhibited mild electrolyte imbalances, with hypomagnesemia (serum magnesium level: 1.4 mg/dL) and low calcium levels (7.1 mg/dL), which were corrected by magnesium sulphate and calcium gluconate.

labs.name: calcium
labs.quote: The patient exhibited mild electrolyte imbalances, with hypomagnesemia (serum magnesium level: 1.4 mg/dL) and low calcium levels (7.1 mg/dL), which were corrected by magnesium sulphate and calcium gluconate.

labs.name: bedside glucose
labs.quote: His bedside glucose was 119 mg/dL, and pupils were normal in size and equally reactive to light.

labs.name: cholinesterase
labs.quote: Cholinesterase levels and the rest of the blood investigations were within normal range (Table 1).

treatment.name: atropine 1 mg IV (ACLS 2020 bradycardia protocol)
treatment.quote: the patient received an immediate 1 mg dose of atropine, resulting in a heart rate increase to 120 beats per minute and a rise in blood pressure to 90/60 mm Hg.

treatment.name: intubation, sedation, gastric lavage
treatment.quote: Subsequently, the patient was intubated, sedated, and underwent gastric lavage.

treatment.name: magnesium sulphate (for hypomagnesemia)
treatment.quote: which were corrected by magnesium sulphate and calcium gluconate.

treatment.name: calcium gluconate (for hypocalcemia)
treatment.quote: which were corrected by magnesium sulphate and calcium gluconate.

treatment.name: conservative ICU management: antibiotics, antacids, thiamine, multivitamins
treatment.quote: The patient received conservative management in the intensive care unit (ICU), including antibiotics, antacids, thiamine, and multivitamins.

cases.outcome: full recovery; regained consciousness after 3 days, extubated, discharged after 7 days of hospitalization
cases.outcome_quote: After three days, he regained consciousness and maintained spontaneous respiration, leading to successful extubation. Following an additional four days of observation and treatment, the patient was discharged with complete recovery.
cases.notes: Co-ingested alcohol. Initially suggested organophosphate poisoning clinically; cholinesterase normal. CT brain normal. No specific antidote used (supportive).
